thread:
Alex Carter: paging now — datadog alerted p99 latency spike for /v1/chat and /v1/completions in us-west1 (~4500ms p99). incident bot paged me at 02:03 UTC. Anyone on rotation? :rotating_light:
Oncall Bot: INCIDENT #3112 triggered by monitor `api.chat.latency.p99` (us-west1). Affected routes: /v1/chat, /v1/completions. Current status: paging -> oncall. Snapshot: p95=320ms, p99=4.5s, error-rate ~0.6%. Links: https://datadog.example/incident/3112 · runbook: https://internal/runbooks/chat-latency.md
Lee Chen: oncall here, looking. I'm pulling the per-model breakdown now.
Jordan Patel: grabbing recent rollout notes — pushed m-neo-2048 quantized yesterday at 00:40 UTC to us-west1 for canary. Could be related.
Maria Singh: heads-up — we saw cache warmup issues with that model during earlier tests. If p99 is high but p95 okay, sounds like tail kv-cache misses or longer token-gen for a subset.
Alex Carter: can we toggle fallback to the smaller m-neo-1024 variant for the chat route in us-west1 for the next 10m while we triage? prefer automated routing change over full rollback.
Jordan Patel: executing route-weight change now.
Jordan Patel: ```
# internal-cli
redwood routes update --route /v1/chat --region us-west1 --model-weights "m-neo-2048:0.2,m-neo-1024:0.8" --note "temp fallback for p99 mitigation"
```
Lee Chen: change applied. Observability: p95 dropped to 280ms within 60s, p99 dropped to ~1.8s down from 4.5s. Error-rate stable. Looks like model tail was the culprit.
Maria Singh: great, that confirms model-specific tail. Can we suppress p99 alerts for 15m so we don't keep paging while this stabilizes? We should also avoid global p99 pages from multi-model routes.
Alex Carter: +1 to suppression window. Also we should change monitors to be per-model/per-route rather than aggregated across all chat traffic. Too much noise.
SRE Rotation: please record the exact monitor IDs and proposed new thresholds. I'll make the post-incident action items.
Jordan Patel: monitor id: dd-monitor-6721 (chat p99 aggregated). Proposed new monitors:
- dd-monitor-6721a: /v1/chat p95 per-route (threshold 400ms)
- dd-monitor-6721b: /v1/chat p99 per-model (m-neo-2048 threshold 2.5s, m-neo-1024 threshold 1.2s)
- dd-monitor-6721c: /v1/completions p99 per-route (threshold 3s)

Also suggest an alert suppression policy for short-lived mitigation windows: 10m auto-snooze when automated fallback is applied.
Maria Singh: here's a draft Datadog query for per-model p99 (feel free to copy/paste):
```
avg:trace.http.request.duration{route:/v1/chat,model:m-neo-2048}.percentile(99) by {model} > 2.5
```
Alex Carter: let's avoid creating 1k monitors. We should make the monitor templated by model label and have a small set of critical-model thresholds in a config file (models.yaml) and fallback to a global default for others.
Lee Chen: logging note — I see repeated KV_CACHE_MISS logs around the same window for m-neo-2048. Dump attached: ```
[2026-03-14T02:02:11Z] request_id=abc123 model=m-neo-2048 kv_cache_miss=true kv_fetch_ms=120
[2026-03-14T02:02:12Z] request_id=abc124 model=m-neo-2048 kv_cache_miss=true kv_fetch_ms=180
```
Jordan Patel: filed a perf task to investigate cache warmup and kv partitioning: https://tracker.internal/RED-9871
SRE Rotation: assigning follow-ups —
- Alex Carter: PR with monitor template + default thresholds -> required by EOD for postmortem (RED-3120)
- Maria Singh: update runbook with model-specific fallback steps and suppression policy (RED-3121)
- Lee Chen: dig deeper into KV cache telemetry and propose kernel/runtime changes if needed (RED-3122)
- Jordan Patel: confirm rollback plan and add automated route-weight play (RED-3123)

Please add owners to each ticket.
Alex Carter: I'll submit the PR to alert-config repo. Quick note in PR: change aggregated p99 -> 99th by model label and add 10m auto-snooze when route-weight changed by automation.
Oncall Bot: Page resolved. Incident #3112 marked as mitigated at 02:12 UTC. Timeline: mitigation=route-weight fallback to m-neo-1024.
Maria Singh: ok, wrap-up — we need to tune thresholds: propose starting per-route p95 targets at observed median+20% and p99 at observed 99th historical baseline * 1.5 for high-variance models. I'll draft numbers tomorrow.
Jordan Patel: PR link: https://git.internal/repos/alert-config/pulls/412 — added templated monitor and suppression rule.
Alex Carter: thanks all. Will follow up in postmortem with data and final thresholds. Next rotation please review the new dashboard panel I added for per-model p99 tail behavior.
SRE Rotation: noted. I'll include this incident in next week's war-room prep. Good job on fast mitigation :thumbsup:
Maria Singh: closing notes — add a short note to the customer-impact section: "no user-facing errors observed; latency degraded for <10% of requests from a small subset of models, mitigated via automated routing". I'll add to the incident doc.
